newsitem.title: GREECE: Banks pull Greek shares lower, OTE part-float ends.
newsitem.headline: Banks pull Greek shares lower, OTE part-float ends.

text.p: Greek shares traded narrowly in subdued volume on Friday as the part-float of state telecoms OTE reached completion and market sentiment benefited from indications of substantial oversubscription.
"The success of OTE's part-float will certainly favour sentiment," said George Athanasakis, an analyst at Alpha Brokerage.
But the broader issue is the attraction of a large number of new investors, both retail and foreign institutionals, through an investment in OTE's low-risk, long-term growth stock, he added.

The book-building for institutional investors in OTE's shares was carried out at 6,200-6,900 drachmas per share, with retail investors subscribing in the public offering at 6,000-6,700 drachmas per share.
The Greek state, currently owner of 92.43 percent of OTE's stock, offers a total of 45 million shares, 10.7 percent.
But another 2.1 million shares is likely to be offered by the state due to strong demand and global co-ordinators will probably allocate an extra 6.33 million shares.
Starting on June 17, OTE will tap the market with a 7.5 percent rights issue of 31.6 million shares at a 16 percent discount to Friday's closing price -- 7,095 drachmas.
The issue price is thus expected to be set at 6,000 drachmas, but formal approval will be granted by shareholders at an extraordinary meeting scheduled for Saturday June 14.
"Investors will focus on corporate news and rely less on broader market sentiment and macroeconomics," Athanasakis said.
This is a time for carefull stock-picking where fundamental analysts have a greater say, he added.
The Athens general index drifted 0.38 percent or 6.17 points lower to settle at 1,625.73 from Thursday's 1,631.90 close.
Industrials edged 0.12 percent forward, but banks were off 0.73 percent, pulling the broader market lower.
Construction continued to trade actively and outperform the market, climbing 3.37 percent.
Turnover wound down ahead of the long weekend holiday, reaching 17.5 billion drachmas on volume of 4.8 million shares.
On Monday June 16 the Athens bourse will remain closed in observation of the Holy Spirit day.
Decliners beat advancers 120 to 97 with 28 shares unchanged on 245 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,119-1,149 drachmas. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, closed down 105 drachmas at 7,095.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 655.64-697.49 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $78.30-$80.01. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,853-4,080 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $15.42-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 258-291 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
